title: Next.js Fundamentals
outcome: Build the Next.js application shell while understanding App Router routing, layouts, Server Components, Client Components, environment boundaries, and rendering behavior.
artifact: A navigable TaskFlow web shell with route groups/layouts, server-first composition, selective client interactivity, and verified environment handling.
labSteps: Generate the web app in the monorepo and verify the development server from the correct workspace.
Create nested routes and a shared layout, then predict which layouts persist across navigation.
Build one component as a Server Component and identify exactly why it can remain server-only.
Add one Client Component for interaction and explain what 'use client' changes in the dependency graph.
Add server-only and public environment values and prove which can reach the browser bundle.
Use browser DevTools and terminal logs to distinguish server rendering from client execution.
failureModes: Adding 'use client' too high in the tree
Accessing browser APIs from Server Components
Using effects for work that belongs in server rendering or a data layer
mastery: Can choose server vs client intentionally
Can debug a hydration or environment-boundary mistake
principles: Use Server Components by default and introduce Client Components only where browser interactivity requires them.
Treat the App Router file system as application structure, not as a place to hide business rules.
Keep secrets and privileged data access on the server side of the Next.js boundary.
Understand caching and rendering behavior before trying to fix stale UI with ad-hoc client state.
